Code style of WorldFloraFast

Source: STYLE.md

WorldFloraFast follows the tidyverse style guide, checked with lintr (configuration in .lintr) and formatted with styler:

styler::style_pkg()      # format the code
lintr::lint_package()    # check it; should report no lints

Recorded decisions

.lintr cannot contain comments, so the decisions it encodes are explained here.

  1. Names of the WorldFlora API are kept. WorldFloraFast keeps the functions and arguments of WorldFlora so that existing scripts keep working. 15 of the 17 exported functions use dots (WFO.match, new.backbone), as do 52 of the 80 argument names, 34 of them with capitals (Fuzzy.min, WFO.data, Genus). These names are not changed. In .lintr, these names match the pattern worldflora_api: names starting with WFO. (exported functions, their arguments such as WFO.data, and internal objects that refer to the backbone, such as WFO.dt), argument names with capitals (Authorship, Genus, Species, Infraspecific, Infraspecific.rank, First.dist, Auth.dist, Old.author.dist, acceptedNameUsageID.match, Fuzzy and Fuzzy.*), and the Darwin Core column names used as arguments of WFO.backbone() (taxonID, scientificName, scientificNameAuthorship, acceptedNameUsageID, taxonomicStatus).
  2. Dotted lower-case names are accepted (dotted.case), the convention of WorldFlora used throughout the code (spec.data, n.found). New code may use snake_case.
  3. Internal functions and constants start with a dot (.fuzzy.one.name(), .HYBRID), so that they are not mistaken for exported functions; and X and FUN, the arguments of .parallel.lapply(), follow the convention of base R’s lapply(). Both match the pattern internal in .lintr. (The patterns use non-capturing groups, (?:...): lintr 3.1 fails on capturing groups in these patterns.)
  4. Line length: 80 characters, as in the style guide, for code, comments and documentation.
  5. Cyclomatic complexity: at most 75 instead of 15. Eight functions are above 15 (.fuzzy.one.name() 73, WFO.one(), WFO.match(), .prepare.one(), WFO.download(), .clean.spec.names(), .genus.epithet(), WFO.prepare()); the limit records the current maximum so that complexity does not grow, and should be lowered as these functions are split.

Names chosen in 1.0.3

  • WFO.backbone() is the name of new.backbone(), consistent with the other functions; new.backbone(), the name in WorldFlora, remains an alias with the same arguments and results (it reads like an S3 method new() for a class “backbone”, which it is not).
  • download_classification() and read_classification(), the only snake_case exported functions (names of the original stand-alone download script), are deprecated in favour of WFO.download() and WFO.read(); they still work, with a warning.
